title: Canary Island Date Palm: Old Date Palms You Can Visit
meta_description: Nice claims the first Canary Island date palm grown outdoors in France, planted in 1864. Four mapped, in Nice, Barcelona and Valencia.
intro: Every Canary Island date palm on the French Riviera arguably descends from one garden on Nice's eastern port, where Baron Vigier is said to have acclimatised the species in France for the first time in 1864. That rests on the garden's own preservation society rather than on any independent record, so take it as the claim it is. The species is easy to admire and impossible to date, because a palm lays down no growth rings to count. Valencia's Palacio de Pineda has a construction date to the year, 1728 to 1731, and its palm has nothing at all; you can order a coffee under it. Barcelona's double row along the Vil.la Amelia avenue produces its own small disagreement, since the city register counts fourteen palms and the garden's chronicler counts fifteen. Valencia's other three stand in a row so recognisable that a bar took their nickname.
